summary: Cefetamet pivoxil is an orally administered prodrug of cefetamet, a third-generation cephalosporin antibiotic. After absorption it is hydrolyzed to active cefetamet, which is bactericidal against many Gram-negative organisms and some Gram-positives. It is used for respiratory tract infections, urinary tract infections, otitis media, pharyngitis/tonsillitis and gonorrhea. It is not FDA-approved; this record is based on EMA/SmPC and reference (BNF/Martindale) information.

Lower respiratory tract infections (acute bronchitis, exacerbations of chronic bronchitis, pneumonia)

admin: Take tablets with food to enhance hydrolysis and absorption of the pivoxil ester
Confirm no history of severe penicillin or cephalosporin allergy before prescribing

moa: Cefetamet is a third-generation cephalosporin that exerts bactericidal activity by binding penicillin-binding proteins and inhibiting the final transpeptidation step of peptidoglycan synthesis in the bacterial cell wall. This blocks cell-wall cross-linking, leading to cell lysis. Like other third-generation agents it has enhanced stability to many beta-lactamases and a broad Gram-negative spectrum. The pivoxil ester is an inactive prodrug hydrolyzed in the intestinal wall to release active cefetamet.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to cefetamet or any cephalosporin
History of severe immediate hypersensitivity (anaphylaxis) to penicillins or other beta-lactams
relative: History of mild penicillin allergy (possible cross-reactivity)
Conditions predisposing to carnitine deficiency (with prolonged pivoxil use)
monitor: Diarrhea suggestive of Clostridioides difficile colitis

preg: There are no adequate controlled studies; cephalosporins as a class are generally regarded as low risk in pregnancy. Use only when the benefit justifies any potential risk.
lact: Cefetamet is excreted into breast milk in small amounts. It is generally considered compatible with breastfeeding, but monitor the infant for diarrhea, thrush or rash.
renal: Cefetamet is eliminated predominantly unchanged by the kidneys; reduce the dose or extend the dosing interval in moderate to severe renal impairment according to creatinine clearance.
hepatic: No specific dose adjustment is generally required for hepatic impairment.

moderate: Probenecid - reduces renal tubular secretion and raises cefetamet levels
Aminoglycosides / loop diuretics - theoretical additive nephrotoxicity (class caution)
minor: Antacids / H2 antagonists - may slightly affect absorption
Valproate (with pivoxil prodrugs) - additive lowering of carnitine
interactions.food: Take with food, which improves absorption of the pivoxil prodrug.
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction expected (no disulfiram-like reaction reported).
interactions.diagnostics: May cause a false-positive Coombs test and false-positive urine glucose with copper-reduction methods (class effect).

rare: Carnitine depletion with prolonged pivoxil use
emergency: Severe persistent bloody diarrhea (C. difficile colitis)

monitoring: Renal function in patients with impairment
Signs of hypersensitivity or skin reaction
Bowel symptoms suggestive of C. difficile colitis
counsel: Take with food and finish the entire course as prescribed
Tell your doctor about any penicillin or cephalosporin allergy before starting
Report any rash, swelling, or difficulty breathing immediately
Report severe or watery/bloody diarrhea, which can occur during or after treatment
Mild stomach upset and loose stools are common; contact your doctor if they are severe or persistent
pk: Antibacterial effect begins within hours of absorption
Peak plasma concentration about 3-4 hours after an oral dose (with food)
Store at room temperature, protected from moisture
pearls: NOT FDA-approved - this record is based on EMA/SmPC and reference (BNF/Martindale) sources; verify against current local product information
Cefetamet pivoxil is an inactive prodrug; take with food to maximize hydrolysis to active cefetamet
Third-generation oral cephalosporin with broad Gram-negative activity
Prolonged use of pivoxil esters can deplete plasma carnitine - relevant for long courses and children
Cross-reactivity is possible in patients with severe beta-lactam allergy
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed one - do not take two doses at once. Complete the full course.
overdose: Overdose may cause nausea, vomiting, epigastric distress and diarrhea; very high levels could theoretically cause CNS irritability or seizures, particularly in renal impairment. Treatment is supportive; cefetamet can be removed by hemodialysis.
